:::{.theorem data-title="Reciprocal Sequence Convergence"}

Assuming that $x_{n}\to x$ as $n \to \infty$ where $x_{n}\neq 0~\forall n$ and
$x\neq 0$. Then:
1. If $1<\beta$ there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if
   $n>N\implies|x_{n}|\geq \frac{|x|}{\beta}$;
2. $\lim_{ n \to \infty }\left(  \frac{1}{x_{n}} \right)= \frac{1}{x}$.

:::

*Proof:*
For (1) we let $\epsilon = \frac{(\beta-1)|x|}{\beta}>0$ and since $x_{n}\to x$
as $n \to \infty$ we have that
$$
\exists N \in \mathbb{N} : \forall n>N,~|x_{n}-x|< \frac{(\beta-1)|x|}{\beta}.
$$
Since, $|x|-|x_{n}|\leq |x_{n}-x|$ we can rearrange the full expression to give
$$
|x|- \frac{{(\beta-1)|x|}}{\beta}<|x_{n}|\implies \frac{|x|}{\beta}<|x_{n}|.
$$
For (2) take $\epsilon>0$ and by part (a), for $\beta=2$
$$
\begin{align}
\exists N_{1}\in \mathbb{N}&:\forall n>N_{1},~|x_{n}|> \frac{|x|}{2}\implies \frac{1}{|x_{n}|}< \frac{2}{|x|} \\ 
\exists N_{2}\in N_{2}&: \forall n>N_{2}, |x_{n}-x|< \frac{|x|^2\epsilon}{2}.
\end{align}
$$
We let $N=\max(N_{1}, N_{2})$ and considering $n>N$ we have that
$$
|x_{n}-x|< \frac{|x|^2\epsilon}{2}\quad\&\quad \frac{1}{|x_{n}|}< \frac{2}{|x|} ,
$$
thus
$$
\left| \frac{1}{x_{n}}- \frac{1}{x}\right|= \left| \frac{{x-x_{n}}}{x x_{n}}\right|= \frac{|x_{n}-x|}{|x| |x_{n}|}<\frac{2|x_{n}-x|}{|x|^2} < \frac{{2|x|^2 \epsilon }}{2} \frac{1}{|x|^2}=\epsilon .
$$
